text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today after climbing sharply yesterday to $137.20, giving back some of those gains. The pullback comes as oil prices stabilized following a volatile week—U.S. crude sits at $91.48 a barrel, up about 9% over the week on escalating Iran-Kuwait military strikes, but those tensions appear to have plateaued rather than intensified further today. The stock had benefited from the week's oil rally, but without fresh geopolitical escalation to push prices higher, some of that momentum eased.

The broader context is that energy stocks like ConocoPhillips are sensitive to both crude prices and market sentiment about conflict duration. While the Iran-Kuwait situation added a supply-risk premium to oil earlier in the week, Trump's comment that renewed hostilities won't last "too long" may have signaled to traders that the acute geopolitical upside for oil prices could be limited, taking some wind out of the energy sector's sails.
